intro: Downtown Toronto has more restaurants than anyone could try in a lifetime, which is exactly why picking one is so hard. These are the long-running favourites we'd send a friend to first — a mix of cheap-and-cheerful classics and a couple of special-occasion splurges.

picks.name: Pai Northern Thai Kitchen
picks.why: Lively, always-busy Northern Thai spot that turned a lot of Torontonians on to khao soi. Expect a wait at peak times.

picks.name: Terroni
picks.why: The Toronto Italian institution: thin-crust pizzas and simple pastas done the same reliable way for decades.

picks.name: Dumpling House
picks.why: No-frills Spadina dumpling shop where you can watch them being folded in the window. Cheap, fast and filling.

picks.name: King's Noodle Restaurant
picks.why: Old-school Cantonese noodle and barbecue house — roast pork and duck hanging in the window, wonton noodles on every table.

picks.name: Buk Chang Dong Soon Tofu
picks.why: Bubbling bowls of soft tofu stew with a spice level you choose. A Bloor Street Koreatown staple for a cold night.

picks.name: Tacos El Asador
picks.why: Tiny, cash-friendly counter famous for its pupusas and tacos. One of the best-value meals downtown.

picks.name: Okonomi House
picks.why: One of the city's oldest Japanese spots, serving savoury okonomiyaki pancakes since the 1970s.

picks.name: Patois
picks.why: Playful Caribbean-meets-Asian comfort food with a loud, fun room. Great for groups who like to share.

picks.name: The Sultan's Tent
picks.why: Moroccan feast in a tented dining room, often with live entertainment — more of an evening than a meal.

picks.name: Sushi Masaki Saito
picks.why: Toronto's most celebrated omakase counter. Very expensive and booked far ahead — this is the once-a-year splurge.
